compiled_state.title: Sprint orchestrator dispatches generic sub-agents for deep-tier review instead of named dso:code-reviewer-* agents
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: During per-worktree review in sprint Phase 5 (per-worktree-review-commit.md Step 2), the sprint orchestrator dispatches review sub-agents using `subagent_type: general-purpose` with the reviewer agent file contents inlined in the prompt, rather than using the named `dso:code-reviewer-*` agent identifiers. This violates CLAUDE.md rule #15: 'Load named dso:code-reviewer-* agent file verbatim for every review — never construct prompts or use generic sub-agents for reviews.'

**Evidence**: During sprint session for epic 2fa0-a2d9-35b7-4101, deep-tier review specialists were dispatched as general-purpose agents with reviewer content inlined. The named agent feedback memory (feedback_named_review_agents.md) requires verbatim loading of the named agent file, not prompt construction.

**Expected**: Review sub-agents must be dispatched using named agent identifiers (`dso:code-reviewer-deep-correctness`, `dso:code-reviewer-deep-hygiene`, `dso:code-reviewer-deep-verification`, `dso:code-reviewer-deep-arch`). The Agent tool's `subagent_type` should match the named agent, not use a generic fallback with inlined content.

**Actual**: `subagent_type: general-purpose` used with reviewer instructions inlined as a prompt string, bypassing the named agent dispatch requirement.

## Impact

Named agent dispatch is enforced for integrity reasons (review gate fabrication prevention, reviewer hash validation). Using generic sub-agents with inlined content may produce findings that fail `record-review.sh` hash validation and bypasses the CLAUDE.md rule intended to prevent orchestrators from fabricating review findings. Also note: the Agent tool's `subagent_type` field only accepts built-in types (general-purpose, claude-code-guide, etc.) — 'dso:code-reviewer-*' are agent file identifiers loaded verbatim into the prompt, not valid subagent_type values. The sprint SKILL.md should be updated to document the correct dispatch pattern: use `subagent_type: general-purpose` but load and pass the NAMED agent file content verbatim (not as a manually constructed prompt).

comments.body: Classification: llm-behavioral. Root cause: commit 558475fed2 replaced correct 'Inline dispatch is mandatory — dso:* labels are agent file identifiers, NOT subagent_type values' with wrong 'Use the registered subagent_type directly — dso:code-reviewer-* are valid Agent tool subagent_type values'. Affected file: plugins/dso/docs/workflows/REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md lines 231-234. The dispatch example at line 298 still correctly shows general-purpose + verbatim content, creating a direct contradiction.
